 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is now probable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Dealing with a sore right hip, Risacher was initially questionable for Saturday’s game. With Cooper Flagg (shoulder) out and Kyrie Irving (knee) downgraded to doubtful, Risacher may have more offensive opportunities. However, Naji Marshall is a better option for managers seeking a streamer. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Naji Marshall (illness) is out for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Marshall started Saturday’s loss to the Spurs, stepping in for Kyrie Irving (knee). His inability to play on Monday will coincide with Irving’s return, so there’s no worthwhile waiver-wire move. 
 Cooper Flagg 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #32 
 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) is questionable for Monday’s game against the Heat. 
 Flagg being listed as questionable on the Mavericks’ initial injury report is good news for fantasy managers. After he sustained a shoulder injury during Friday’s win over the Pacers, expectations were that the reigning Rookie of the Year would miss a few days. Now, Flagg could miss just one game after sitting out Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. If he returns, Zaccharie Risacher will head to the bench. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher recorded 11 points (4-of-8 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, two assists, one steal, two blocks and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 After Cooper Flagg sustained a left shoulder injury in Friday’s win over the Pacers, Risacher started for the Mavericks for the first time on Saturday. He had a highlight-worthy block on Victor Wembanyama at the rim in the first half, but his overall production wasn’t enough to put Risacher on the streaming radar. Naji Marshall and PJ Washington (12 points, four rebounds and two assists) are better fantasy options until Flagg returns. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 Naji Marshall produced 10 points (4-of-8 FGs, 1-of- 3 FTs), four rebounds, five assists, one steal and one three-pointer in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs. 
 With Kyrie Irving and Cooper Flagg unavailable, Marshall moved into the starting lineup for Saturday’s game. He took on playmaking responsibilities for large stretches of the 122-106 defeat, dishing out five of the 12 assists recorded by Mavericks starters. While Irving should be back for Monday’s game against the Heat, Flagg’s shoulder injury may keep him out for multiple games. If so, Marshall is worth streaming in deep leagues. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 Naji Marshall, Max Christie, Zaccharie Risacher, PJ Washington and Daniel Gafford will start Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 The Mavericks won’t have Cooper Flagg or Kyrie Irving on Saturday, with the former facing an extended absence after injuring his shoulder during Friday’s win over the Pacers. As a result, Marshall and Risacher will start, with Naji offering a higher ceiling for fantasy managers seeking a streamer. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is available for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Risacher is officially available for Saturday’s game. Cooper Flagg and Kyrie Irving’s absences don’t guarantee more usage for Risacher, but his minutes may increase because of the injuries. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher (hip) is questionable for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Risacher had 11 points off the bench in Friday’s win over the Pacers. With the Mavericks’ lengthy injury report, he could play at least 30 minutes again, though he’s probably not worth streaming in most fantasy leagues. 
 Zaccharie Risacher 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #10 
 Zaccharie Risacher scored 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), six rebounds, an assist, a steal, three blocks, and a three in 32 minutes against the Pacers. 
 He started the first half with 11 points and ended the game with 11 points. Risacher took advantage of all the easy opportunities in front of him. He got out in transition and took efficient shots. It seems like the Mavs are really prioritizing him and will get ample opportunities this season, even if it’s not a starter. Dusty May likes to play players with length, skill, and athleticism and Risacher can fit that. 
 Caleb Martin 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #16 
 Caleb Martin (thumb) has been ruled out against the Rockets on Wednesday. 
 Martin will start the season on the injury report. However, Dallas has more than enough depth in the frontcourt to make up for his absence. Naji Marshall and Zaccharie Risacher may take on a few extra minutes. 
 Naji Marshall 
 DAL 
 Forward 
 #3 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports Naji Marshall has agreed to a three-year, $52.2 million extension with the Mavericks. 
 Marshall is entering his third season in Dallas and is now set to be tied to the team until 2030. The two best scoring seasons of his career have come during his time with the Mavericks, and his veteran presence will be important as they continue to add young talent. Marshall has stepped up when Dallas has dealt with injuries in the frontcourt, and he’ll likely continue to be a valuable reserve option for them next season.

 P.J. Washington lit up the Heat with 20 points (6-of-15 FGs), nine rebounds, two assists, two steals, one block and four three-pointers on Monday.
 Washington has been a solid source of offense for Dallas early on this season. This was his second 20-point game of the season, and he has averaged 15.5 points and 2.0 triples per game thus far. He has been a decent source of steals in years past, and he finally got his first two of the season in this game. That number should regulate, allowing him to be a better fantasy producer moving forward.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Cooper Flagg

 Cooper Flagg (shoulder) returned to the lineup on Monday and finished with 29 points (12-of-23 FGs), six rebounds, 11 assists, four steals, two blocks, two three-pointers and five turnovers in a 113-109 win over the Heat.
 The initial expectation was that this would be a multi-game absence for Flagg. However, it only ended up being one game on the sidelines for him, and he returned in a big way in this game. The only knock on Flagg so far this season has been the high turnover numbers, but he has been truly fantastic in every other category. Of course, the sample size is small, but if he continues to produce at this level, he will have absolutely been worth taking in the first round of fantasy drafts.
 -  Noah Rubin

 Anthony Edwards 
 MIN

 Anthony Edwards accounted for 47 points (19-of-33 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, two blocks and five three-pointers in Monday’s loss to the Cavaliers.
 Initially questionable for Monday’s game due to right knee injury management, Edwards played 41 of a possible 53 minutes in the overtime defeat. He was lethal inside the arc, shooting 14-of-18 from two. Edwards hit just 5-of-15 from three, but his mid-range and paint scoring boosted his overall field-goal percentage. The Timberwolves star now has two of the NBA’s top four scoring nights this season, with Luka Dončić’s 52-point effort against the Jazz at the top.
